requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1 (survives reboot, starts automatically)
requirements.summary: iptables/ip6tables installed, rules saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save(6), added to default OpenRC runlevel. A genuine reboot was performed (boot_id changed from 2bea8e68... to ef2bf38a..., cross-checked against the fixed global boot-identity snapshots). Post-reboot, rc-service reports iptables, ip6tables, and sshd all 'started' with identical INPUT chain rules intact, demonstrating the full baseline->disruption->recovery transition required for persistence claims.
INPUT chain includes ACCEPT for tcp dport 22. Functional nc connectivity test confirms port 22 reachable both before and after the reboot.
INPUT chain includes ACCEPT for tcp dport 8080. A local nc listener on 8080 was reachable in functional tests both pre- and post-reboot.

INPUT policy set to DROP with an explicit REJECT (icmp-port-unreachable) catch-all rule after the allow rules. A functional test against port 9999 failed/was rejected both before and after the reboot, confirming unrelated inbound traffic is blocked.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — a persistent firewall on node1 permitting SSH and TCP 8080 while rejecting other inbound traffic — are satisfied with direct, corroborated evidence including a real reboot (boot_id change cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots) and matching functional connectivity tests before and after. Hygiene is good; only a trivial leftover log file was found, and temporary test listeners were properly cleaned up.
limitations: The firewall also allows inbound ICMP echo-request (ping) on both IPv4 and IPv6, which is outside the literal 'SSH and TCP 8080 only' wording, though this is a common and low-risk diagnostic allowance rather than an open service port.

Functional connectivity tests were run from the node itself against its own address rather than from an external client, so cross-network reachability was not independently observed, though this is standard practice for this kind of check within the available tooling.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: package install, rule configuration (IPv4 and IPv6, a reasonable superset of the requirement), OpenRC enablement, rule save, and a bounded reboot to prove persistence. Two temporary nc listeners on port 8080 (cmd-04b72e78582c4431, cmd-6c9d08d5de6a4a75) were started purely for functional testing and both were killed with pkill nc in the same or a following command (cmd-f79a03fcd8a54c27, cmd-6c9d08d5de6a4a75) — no lingering process. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small artifact left by the backgrounded reboot command (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot); it is trivial, non-sensitive, and does not affect firewall functionality. No failed or conflicting services, no weakened security controls, and no unexplained mutations were found in the command trace.
